We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z \geq -1.16).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/cac32ab36217820b63574e011488721bf57652fa63b4cbb7e5029fb54ce26243.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-P(Z<-1.16) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.16)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/48adcb6bd3b0d12b9bc935b2414d615e0014d905b89a9f7d632306cd30f08580.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(-1.16) =  0.1230.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-Φ(-1.16) \\  & =1-0.1230 \\  & =0.8770.\end{aligned}
$$
